text: Stock market restructuring puts corporate governance in focus

HÀ NỘI - Companies listed on the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) are expected to transfer to the Hochiminh Stock Exchange (HoSE) by the end of 2026 under Việt Nam's stock market restructuring plan, with the two exchanges coordinating the process to ensure trading continuity and protect investors' rights.
Vũ Thị Thúy Nga, general director of HNX, announced the roadmap at the exchange's 2026 annual corporate conference in Hà Nội on November 10.

She said the transfer represented a transition within Việt Nam's unified stock market, adding that HNX would work closely with HoSE to ensure the process proceeded smoothly without affecting shareholders and investors.
Over the years, many businesses have chosen HNX as their first platform for accessing capital markets and gradually developing their scale, governance capacity and transparency.
For companies registered on the UPCoM market, HNX will continue supporting improvements in information disclosure and corporate governance while helping them prepare for further development.

Nguyễn Hoàng Dương, vice chairman of the State Securities Commission (SSC), said the reorganisation of stock trading markets was part of the broader plan developed by the SSC and the Ministry of Finance.
Under the proposed structure, HoSE will focus on stock trading and organise shares into different trading boards, with classification criteria expected to be announced soon.
HNX will concentrate on Government and corporate bond markets, derivatives and research into new markets, including a dedicated market for innovative start-ups.
It will also continue operating UPCoM, providing a platform for companies to prepare for official listing.
Dương called on companies transferring from HNX to HoSE to work closely with both exchanges and complete the necessary preparations in line with regulations and the implementation schedule.
He also urged the exchanges to modernise their infrastructure, strengthen service capacity and maintain safe, uninterrupted trading.

From the corporate side, Nguyễn Xuân Ngọc, a member of the Board of Directors of PetroVietnam Technical Services Corporation (PTSC), said the company had reviewed its governance and management systems and updated internal regulations after receiving notice of the planned transfer.
PTSC's board had also instructed the company to review its information disclosure systems and test connectivity with HoSE, with support from HNX.

Ngọc said moving to HoSE would create more favourable conditions for the company to access international capital and professional investment funds, making investor relations and information disclosure increasingly important.
PTSC has published bilingual reports since 2005-2006, while work related to environmental, social and governance (ESG) matters is currently under way.
With support from the two exchanges, the company has not encountered major difficulties in preparing for the transfer, he said.
Dương said improving the quality of listed and registered companies must go hand in hand with stronger corporate governance, financial reporting and information transparency.
These are not only regulatory requirements but also necessary for companies to improve their competitiveness.
Following Việt Nam's upgrade to emerging market status, he said, attracting and retaining large, long-term foreign capital flows would depend on companies' preparedness and competitiveness.

International institutions and foreign investors look beyond market size and growth rates to assess corporate governance, business ethics, transparency, the reliability of financial statements, audit quality, equal access to information, English-language disclosures and investor protection mechanisms.

Dương called on the exchanges and relevant organisations to review regulations on corporate governance, financial reporting, auditing and information disclosure and identify areas requiring legal and policy changes.

He also proposed mechanisms to encourage companies to adopt good corporate governance practices, including scoring and classification systems that take governance quality into account when assigning stocks to trading boards and constructing market indices.
Training and guidance on corporate governance, English-language disclosure and the adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards were also highlighted.
For companies, Dương urged stronger internal governance and a shift away from treating information disclosure as a procedural obligation.
Instead, it should be viewed as a tool for improving corporate quality and attracting investment.
Businesses should also proactively adopt good governance practices, publish information in English and incorporate sustainability indicators into their business strategies. - BIZHUB/VNS
